name: The Madore Beaubien household
head: beaubien_madore

arrival.note: He is licensed to sell goods at Chicago in 1831 and a resident thereafter. His birth and early years belong to the family's Chicago period from 1812 and are not dated here. THE SETTLERS TABLE PRINTS NO YEAR FOR HIM AND THE ABSENCE IS READ AS AN ABSENCE. Row bk_mose1_as_005 leaves the year cell empty where every other row in the column carries a year or a ditto, which is what a native's row looks like; it therefore offers nothing to date this field with and the 1831 licence stands as the reading it always was.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

origin.note: A DRAWN REGION IS REPLACED BY A PRINTED NATIVITY, AND THE OLD VALUE WAS WRONG ABOUT A MAN BORN HERE. This field held 'The Mid-Atlantic states', drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a survivorship sample, carrying `replaceable_by` 'a source that says where this household came from'. This is that source. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830 (data/research/books/records/moses_kirkland_v1_actual_settlers_pre_1830.json). It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. Row bk_mose1_as_005 reads 'Beaubien, Medore Benj' — the scan sets the j as a bracket — nativity CHICAGO, remarks 'Voted in 1830', AND NO YEAR CELL. THE BLANK IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE FINDING: it is the only empty year in a column running 1804 to 1829 that is not a ditto, and a man born at the settlement has no year of arrival to print. The card's own arrival note already says his birth and early years belong to the family's Chicago period from 1812, so the table and the record agree and the drawn region contradicted both. INFERRED AND NOT ATTESTED for the reason the whole table is: 1895, at second hand, transcription_mediated. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's own preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and its remarks are civic acts of 1825-1830. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here.

reason_for_coming.value: A store for the traffic of a town filling up
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as merchant, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

kin.note: MADORE BEAUBIEN IS THE SON OF COL. JEAN BAPTISTE BEAUBIEN, AND HIS OWN CARD HAS SAID SO IN PROSE SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN: 'He is the son of Jean Baptiste Beaubien by his first wife Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman' — Andreas, History of Chicago vol. 1, the same reading that grades the rest of that card. NOTHING IS UPGRADED HERE. The claim was already attested on the card and already cited to andreas_1884_v1; this row only puts it where a query can reach it, because a sentence in a note is not a relationship any tool can read. THE IDENTIFICATION IS NOT A SURNAME MATCH: the town holds one Jean Baptiste Beaubien, the card names him with all three forenames and a rank, and the 1831 county licence Andreas prints has Madore selling goods 'alongside Alexander Robinson and his father'. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: his mother Mah-naw-bun-no-quah is not a person in this dataset and no row is written for her, and this row says nothing about where either man lived.

dated_bounds.note: A BOUND ON PRESENCE, AND NOTHING FURTHER. Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 records a man who presented himself and voted, so the entry places a body in Chicago no later than 1834-08-11. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes: a man on a roll of 1833, 1834 or 1835 is not thereby at Chicago on 1 July 1835. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT. The reading of the roll is documented — the town's own paper, held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository, twice mediated by Schulz's transcription and Genealogy Trails' republication, which this project has not gone behind. What no source states is that the man on the roll is the person on this card: data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json joins them on a name, by its rule “one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 8 bearer(s) of the surname were considered.”, and forenames agree initial for initial: entry 'Madore Beaubien' against resident 'Madore Benjamin Beaubien'. A bound whose subject is inferred is an inferred bound. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: ELECTED ONE OF THE FIVE FIRST TRUSTEES OF THE TOWN on 10 August 1833 with 23 of 28 votes - the third-highest poll. He is the son of Jean Baptiste Beaubien by his first wife Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman, which makes him the only person in this parcel who is both a documented office-holder of the incorporated town and a documented member of a Native family. THE RECORD STATES THAT AND STOPS THERE. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Beaubien, Madore” (poll_1834_010, line 179). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 20 under 30', one of its male bands, conditioned on `civic_list_20_and_over` because the person stands on a poll, a tax list or a muster roll.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('beaubien_madore:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a poll, tax or muster list names a person 20 or over - the 1840 schedule's own adult line. THE FRANCHISE'S AGE RULE IS NOT IN ANY SOURCE RECORD THIS PROJECT HOLDS; this is the model's conditioning and not a reading (T-1303's finding, handed to T-1304). No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: A TOWN TRUSTEE, A MERCHANT AND A MAN WHOSE MOTHER WAS OTTAWA, in a town that was six weeks from the final removal of the Potawatomi when this scene is set. That combination is the reason this household carries the review flag: nothing in the record is improvised, and nothing about it can be treated as closed without the consultation AGENTS.md requires. The documented facts are the office, the trade, the licence, the house and the parentage; the record adds nothing to them.
